extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy (esp. epistemology/empiricism); philosophers and scholars evaluating claims of innate ideas
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and tests for judging whether ideas or principles are innate rather than acquired, as argued in a philosophical treatise (empiricist perspective). Useful for evaluating claims about innate concepts, propositions, or moral principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles not innate, unless their Ideas be innate
rubrics_metrics.description: Had those who would persuade us that there are innate principles not taken them together in gross, but considered separately the parts out of which those propositions are made... For, if the IDEAS which made up those truths were not, it was impossible that the PROPOSITIONS made up of them should be innate...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test claims of innate propositions by checking whether the component ideas are themselves present innately. If constituent ideas are not innate, the compound proposition cannot be innate. Examine the mental availability of the basic ideas before treating higher-order propositions as innate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas, especially those belonging to Principles, not born with children
rubrics_metrics.description: If we will attentively consider new-born children, we shall have little reason to think that they bring many ideas into the world with them... there is not the least appearance of any settled ideas at all in them; especially of IDEAS ANSWERING THE TERMS WHICH MAKE UP THOSE UNIVERSAL PROPOSITIONS THAT ARE ESTEEMED INNATE PRINCIPLES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at the mental state of newborns and very young children: innate ideas should be evident at birth or very early infancy. Absence of settled ideas in infants is evidence against innateness of those concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impossibility and Identity not innate ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is impossible for the same thing to be, and not to be,” is certainly (if there be any such) an innate PRINCIPLE. But can any one think... that “impossibility” and “identity” are two innate IDEAS? Are they such as all mankind have, and bring into the world with them?...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether purportedly innate abstract ideas (e.g., impossibility, identity) are actually present in children or universally evident. If such abstract concepts are not primary in childhood experience, they are unlikely to be innate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity, an Idea not innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: If IDENTITY (to instance that alone) be a native impression... I would gladly be resolved by any one of seven, or seventy years old, whether a man, being a creature consisting of soul and body, be the same man when his body is changed?... it will appear that our idea of SAMENESS is not so settled and clear as to deserve to be thought innate in us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the idea of 'sameness' is clear, distinct, and universally shared; disagreement and conceptual confusion about identity indicate non-innateness. Use ordinary examples (personal identity, historical figures) to probe clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: What makes the same man?
rubrics_metrics.description: He that shall with a little attention reflect on the resurrection... will find it perhaps not easy to resolve with himself, what makes the same man, or wherein identity consists; and will not be forward to think he, and every one, even children themselves, have naturally a clear idea of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use difficult real or theological cases (resurrection, soul-body distinctions) to test if 'identity' is an innate, straightforward idea; if people struggle to answer, that suggests the idea is acquired and complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole and Part not innate ideas.
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us examine that principle of mathematics, viz. THAT THE WHOLE IS BIGGER THAN A PART... I am sure it has as good a title as any to be thought so; which yet nobody can think it to be, when he considers the ideas it comprehends in it, WHOLE and PART, are perfectly relative; but the positive ideas to which they properly and immediately belong are extension and number...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For relational principles (whole/part), check whether their underlying primary ideas (e.g., extension, number) are themselves innate. If relations presuppose non-innate bases, the relation cannot be innate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of Worship not innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: That GOD IS TO BE WORSHIPPED, is, without doubt, as great a truth as any that can enter into the mind of man... But yet it can by no means be thought innate, unless the ideas of GOD and WORSHIP are innate. That the idea the term worship stands for is not in the understanding of children...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical or moral maxims (e.g., duty to worship) require the corresponding practical concepts (God, worship) to be present innately. If children lack the notion of worship or its elements, the practical principle cannot be innate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of God not innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: If any idea can be imagined innate, the idea of GOD may... Without a notion of a law-maker, it is impossible to have a notion of a law, and an obligation to observe it. Besides the atheists... hath not navigation discovered... whole nations... among whom there was to be found no notion of a God, no religion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test cross-cultural presence: if entire peoples lack any notion of God, that counts strongly against the idea being innate. Innateness would imply universality irrespective of upbringing or geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: The name of God not universal or obscure in meaning.
rubrics_metrics.description: But had all mankind everywhere a notion of a God... the idea of him was not innate. For, though no nation were to be found without a name, and some few dark notions of him, yet that would not prove them to be natural impressions on the mind; no more than the names of fire, or the sun, heat, or number, do prove the ideas they stand for to be innate...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish linguistic universality from conceptual innateness: the presence of a name across cultures does not prove the underlying idea is innate; investigate whether the concept exists independently of language and upbringing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas of God and idea of Fire.
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of God being once mentioned... the suitableness of such a notion to the principles of common reason, and the interest men will always have to mention it often, must necessarily spread it far and wide... yet the general reception of this name... prove not the idea to be innate; but only that they who made the discovery had made a right use of their reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how natural reasoning and social transmission can propagate a concept widely; widespread acceptance due to reason or instruction does not equal innateness. Examine transmission and explanatory power rather than mere prevalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of God not innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: This is all could be inferred from the notion of a God, were it to be found universally in all the tribes of mankind... For the generality of the acknowledging of a God... which, if it be sufficient to prove the idea of God innate, will as well prove the idea of fire innate...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistency checks: if universality were the sole criterion, many non-innate ideas (like fire) would qualify. Be skeptical of broad inferences from general acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitable to God’s goodness, that all Men should have an idea of Him, therefore naturally imprinted by Him, answered.
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeed it is urged, that it is suitable to the goodness of God, to imprint upon the minds of men characters and notions of himself... This argument, if it be of any force, will prove much more than those who use it in this case expect... I think it a very good argument to say,—the infinitely wise God hath made it so; and therefore it is best. But it seems to me a little too much confidence of our own wisdom to say,—‘I think it best; and therefore God hath made it so.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge teleological or theological arguments for innateness: appeal to divine goodness does not constitute empirical evidence of imprinting. Require observable markers (clarity, universality, distinctness) rather than normative appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas of God various in different Men.
rubrics_metrics.description: I grant that if there were any ideas to be found imprinted on the minds of men, we have reason to expect it should be the notion of his Maker... But how late is it before any such notion is discoverable in children? And when we find it there, how much more does it resemble the opinion and notion of the teacher, than represent the true God?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine variability across individuals and the influence of education: if adult conceptions more closely match teachers' views than a putative innate idea, that suggests acquisition through instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrary and inconsistent ideas of God under the same name.
rubrics_metrics.description: Can it be thought that the ideas men have of God are the characters and marks of himself, engraven in their minds by his own finger, when we see that, in the same country, under one and the same name, men have far different, nay often contrary and inconsistent ideas and conceptions of him?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single term corresponds to widely divergent and contradictory concepts among members of the same culture, this undermines the claim of a single innate idea behind the term. Investigate intra-linguistic conceptual inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross ideas of God.
rubrics_metrics.description: What true or tolerable notion of a Deity could they have, who acknowledged and worshipped hundreds? Every deity that they owned above one was an infallible evidence of their ignorance of Him, and a proof that they had no true notion of God... the universality of consent... will as much prove the name as not the idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the content quality of widely held beliefs: crude, anthropomorphic, or polytheistic conceptions across peoples argue against an innate, accurate notion of God. Evaluate sophistication, not mere presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of God not innate although wise men of all nations come to have it.
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be said, that wise men of all nations came to have true conceptions of the unity and infinity of the Deity, I grant it. But then this... excludes universality of consent in anything but the name... it seems to me plainly to prove, that the truest and best notions men have of God were not imprinted, but acquired by thought and meditation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between conclusions reached by considered reflection versus innate knowledge: if only a small minority (wise men) reach refined conceptions by reasoning, that supports acquisition through thought, not innate imprinting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Odd, low, and pitiful ideas of God common among men.
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk but with country people... though the name of God be frequently in their mouths, yet the notions they apply this name to are so odd, low, and pitiful, that nobody can imagine they were taught by a rational man; much less that they were characters written by the finger of God himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-check ordinary beliefs among unreflective or uneducated people: prevalence of crude misconceptions indicates social transmission and error, not innate clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: If the Idea of God be not innate, no other can be supposed innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: Since then though the knowledge of a God be the most natural discovery of human reason, yet the idea of him is not innate... I imagine there will be scarce any other idea found that can pretend to it... I must own, as far as I can observe, I can find none, and would be glad to be informed by any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the most promising candidate (idea of God) as a touchstone: if even that fails tests for innateness, be skeptical about any other claimed innate ideas. Apply the same empirical and conceptual tests broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea of Substance not innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: I confess there is another idea which would be of general use for mankind to have, as it is of general talk as if they had it; and that is the idea of SUBSTANCE; which we neither have nor can have by sensation or reflection... we signify nothing by the word SUBSTANCE but only an uncertain supposition of we know not what.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For metaphysical concepts like 'substance', test whether they are derivable from sensation/reflection; if not obtainable by these faculties, they are unlikely to be innate in the clear sense claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Propositions can be innate, since no Ideas are innate.
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever then we talk of innate, either speculative or practical, it may with as much probability be said, that a man hath 100 pounds sterling in his pocket... as to think that certain PROPOSITIONS are innate when the IDEAS about which they are can by no means be supposed to be so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If basic ideas fail innateness tests, any compound propositions built from them also fail. Prioritize demonstration of basic idea-innateness before accepting innate propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No innate Ideas in the Memory.
rubrics_metrics.description: To which let me add: if there be any innate ideas, any ideas in the mind which the mind does not actually think on, they must be lodged in the memory; and from thence must be brought into view by remembrance... Whenever the memory brings any idea into actual view, it is with a consciousness that it had been there before...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the phenomenology of memory as a test: innate ideas, if truly pre-existing, should be remembered (i.e., bring a consciousness of prior acquaintance) when they come to mind. Lack of such recollective awareness argues against innateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles not innate, because of little use or little certainty.
rubrics_metrics.description: Besides what I have already said, there is another reason why I doubt that neither these nor any other principles are innate... those that are pretended innate, and concern SPECULATION, are of no great use; and those that concern PRACTICE, not self-evident; and neither of them distinguishable from some other truths not allowed to be innate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that innate principles be both useful and clearly distinguishable from acquired truths; principles of negligible use or uncertain status are unlikely candidates for being innate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of Men’s Discoveries depends upon the different Application of their Faculties.
rubrics_metrics.description: To conclude: some ideas forwardly offer themselves to all men’s understanding... The great difference that is to be found in the notions of mankind is, from the different use they put their faculties to... OUR KNOWLEDGE DEPENDS UPON THE RIGHT USE OF THOSE POWERS NATURE HATH BESTOWED UPON US, and how little upon SUCH INNATE PRINCIPLES AS ARE IN VAIN SUPPOSED TO BE IN ALL MANKIND FOR THEIR DIRECTION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether variation in knowledge is better explained by differential exercise of faculties and experience rather than by presence/absence of innate principles. Favor explanations invoking learning and use over innate endowments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Men must think and know for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.description: What censure doubting thus of innate principles may deserve... Truth has been my only aim... perhaps we should make greater progress in the discovery of rational and contemplative knowledge, if we sought it in the fountain, IN THE CONSIDERATION OF THINGS THEMSELVES; and made use rather of our own thoughts than other men’s to find it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological prescription: evaluate claims of innateness by direct examination of things and personal consideration rather than appeal to authority or received opinion. Encourage independent inquiry as a test of whether ideas are self-evident or learned.
